newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Tokyo stocks fall as Hong Kong shares strengthen.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo stocks fall as Hong Kong shares strengthen.

text.p: Tokyo stocks fell on financial-sector jitters on Wednesday while in Hong Kong shares were lifted by a strong overnight showing on Wall Street.
Elsewhere in Asia, shares in Taiwan and Australia closed solidly up.
Japanese shares were battered after a bank said it suspected one of its former employees misused funds, brokers said. Futures-linked selling also pushed Japanese shares lower.
The key Nikkei 225 average tumbled 276.41 points, or 1.32 percent, to 20,681.67. Its December futures fell 250 points to finish at 20,690.
"The market was in a wait-and-see mood, foreign investors were net sellers and then news of financial trouble at a bank emerged to depress the market further," one broker said.
News that Biwako Bank suspected a former employee of improperly using bank funds knocked the market lower.
Selling by foreigners also helped to erode gains made earlier in the week. The recent slide in the yen has cut into the value of foreigners' yen-denominated investments.
"It is difficult for domestic investors to buy when foreign investors are in a net selling stance," said Harushige Kobayashi, deputy general manager at Yamaichi Securities.
Hong Kong stocks were helped by New York's Dow Jones index which finished at 6007, up 34 points on Tuesday, and from expiration of October Hang Seng index futures, brokers said.
The Hang Seng Index closed 213.30 points higher at 12,405.47.
"The rise is a combination of demand stimulated by U.S. market gains and futures expiration," said Anthony Mak, sales director at Vickers Ballas."

Taiwan stocks emerged from weeks of bearish trading with a late rally sparked by buying in plastics and textiles shares. The weighted index closed 66.42 points or 1.04 percent higher. Before Wednesday, the index had lost over 200 points in October.
"It is simply market psychology and Tuesday's big drop may have triggered some bargain hunting action," Joe Chiou, a securities analyst for Taiwan Securities Investment, said.
Australian shares rose on strength among banks which had benefited from a bond market rally after U.S. Treasuries surged on Tuesday.
The All Ordinaries index closed 13.7 points higher at 2,336.7.

"The banks have been getting a boost from the bond market once every two or three days," Jamie Spiteri, a dealer at Sydney-based broker, Shaw Stockbroking, said . "I don't see any change to this situation in the near term."
The dollar stayed just above 114 yen in Tokyo after gains in early trade were eroded by active profit-taking by U.S. operators and some Japanese trust banks.
At 1115 GMT the dollar was trading at 114.35/4.40 yen and 1.5109/15 marks.
Gold ended little changed in Hong Kong from its New York close. Bullion was at US$380.40/380.90 an ounce vs New York's US$380.35/85 close on Tuesday.
In Singapore oil prices extended losses. December Brent crude oil futures traded at $23.50 per barrel, down 24 cents from the London settlement on Tuesday.
